title: Architectural approach for Interactive 3D Cyber-Grid Retro-Tech Landing Page
context: The project requires a high-fidelity 3D environment featuring a wireframe model with specific aesthetic effects (neon glow, glitching, and scanlines). To achieve this while maintaining performance and scalability, a robust 3D engine is required to handle the scene graph, animation loops, and custom shader effects.
decision: Utilize Three.js as the primary 3D engine to render the wireframe model and handle the Y-axis rotation. Implement custom GLSL shaders for the 'Cyber-Grid' neon effects and the 'glitch' logic to ensure high performance. The UI components (Glassmorphic Navigation and System Status) will be implemented as a separate DOM/CSS layer overlaid on the canvas to ensure UI responsiveness and ease of styling.
alternativesConsidered: Vanilla WebGL: Rejected due to high complexity and significant development overhead for basic 3D geometry and lighting.
Spline/Babylon.js: Rejected because Three.js offers the most mature ecosystem for custom shader passes required for the specific 'glitch' and 'scanline' requirements.

positive: Modular shader implementation allows for easy adjustment of 'glitch' intensity.
Decoupled UI layer ensures that navigation and status panels remain responsive regardless of 3D scene complexity.
negative: Increased initial bundle size due to the inclusion of the Three.js library.
risks: Potential frame rate drops on low-end mobile devices during complex shader calculations.
Potential issues with depth testing when overlaying 2D UI elements over 3D space if not handled via a separate layer.
